analysis.title: Emerging Markets Insights: Big Tech AI Spending, November 2026
key_insights: Several US cloud giants missed Q3 earnings estimates, each for its own reasons, but their future spending plans did not change. Combined capex is expected to exceed US$870 billion in 2026 and US$1.3 trillion in 2027.
The AI model build-out has boosted sales of Asian chip makers. Chip demand exceeds supply, so these firms have raised prices, and Asian chipmakers report output sold out through 2029.
Smaller data-centre firms are finding it hard to raise capital and may have to cancel orders. US cloud giants are likely to take over that capacity because they expect strong future demand.

Lula won the Brazilian presidential runoff, which few expected. Brazilian stocks fell sharply. Investors now expect Brazilian interest rates to rise rather than fall, and the currency outlook has worsened.

In Brazil the selloff may create individual stock opportunities. The firm is screening on company strength, debt levels, cashflow and ability to handle shocks, and prefers exporters and commodity firms because a weaker currency can lift their earnings.

A majority of EM firms have reported Q3 results. Analysts expect profits 70% higher than a year ago (source: Goldman Sachs, as of October 30, 2026). Technology-heavy North Asian markets are again expected to lead.
The firm is watching for strength in sectors and countries outside North Asia. Better-than-expected results there could lift share prices and spread gains across more markets and sectors.

EM stocks fell in October as technology stocks came under pressure again. Investors questioned whether heavy AI spending would produce adequate returns, and rising interest rates raised concerns about how it would be financed.

Emerging Asia declined with most major markets lower, and South Korean semiconductor stocks were particularly weak. Indian equities rose as investors moved from AI infrastructure stocks into software services businesses, and Indian IT companies performed well.
Coordinated drone and missile attacks against Saudi Arabia weakened sentiment across the Middle East. Mexican equities rose despite inflation concerns.

The firm remains constructive on EM but favours a selective approach. Higher US interest rates and a stronger US dollar may cause volatility, though many EM companies have low debt, strong cash levels and some US dollar-linked revenue.
The firm is watching AI spending closely because higher yields could raise the cost of future investment.

sector_views.rationale: Demand exceeds supply, prices have been raised, and output is reported sold out through 2029. US cloud capex plans are unchanged.
A weaker currency can boost their earnings after the post-election selloff.
Investors moved from AI infrastructure stocks into software services businesses in October, and Indian IT companies performed well.

earnings_insights: Several US cloud giants missed Q3 estimates (reported, vs consensus), each for its own reasons. The report does not name the companies or give figures.
Analysts expect EM profits to be 70% higher than a year ago (forecast, per Goldman Sachs as of October 30, 2026), with a majority of EM firms having reported Q3.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Spending plans were unchanged despite Q3 earnings misses, which supports demand for Asian chip makers.
Planned spending keeps rising, which supports Asian chip demand but raises financing sensitivity to higher yields.
Analyst expectation, led by technology-heavy North Asia.
Higher borrowing costs for Brazilian firms after the Lula win.
Higher US rates and a stronger dollar may cause EM volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: US cloud giants kept spending plans unchanged at over US$870 billion in 2026 and US$1.3 trillion in 2027. Asian chipmakers report output sold out through 2029 and have raised prices.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors questioned whether heavy AI spending will produce adequate returns, and rising rates raised concerns about financing it. Smaller data-centre firms struggle to raise capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher yields raising the cost of future investment enough to change spending plans, which the firm says it is watching.
